ip_top_stories.title: Eleonora Rosati, lawyer: 'Artists are already thinking about how to protect themselves from AI; Taylor Swift has registered her voice'
ip_top_stories.summary: IP lawyer Eleonora Rosati discusses how artists, including Taylor Swift, are taking proactive legal steps to protect their voices and likenesses from AI exploitation. The interview covers the novel legal strategies emerging as artists seek to register and assert rights over their personal attributes in the face of AI-generated content.

ip_top_stories.title: Big Tech Is a Thief and a Liar, Says New York Times Publisher
ip_top_stories.summary: The publisher of the New York Times has publicly accused Big Tech companies of theft and dishonesty in relation to the use of news content for AI training. The statement comes amid the ongoing high-stakes litigation between the NYT and OpenAI, framing the dispute as a fundamental issue of copyright and fair compensation for publishers.

ip_top_stories.title: AI Deepfake Law NO FAKES Act Advances in Congress With Key Senate Committee Vote
ip_top_stories.summary: The NO FAKES Act, US federal legislation aimed at protecting individuals' voices and likenesses from AI-generated deepfakes, has cleared a key Senate committee vote. The bill would create a federal right for individuals to control digital replicas of themselves, representing a significant legislative development for AI and intellectual property policy.

ip_top_stories.title: Investors sue Adobe execs over AI copyright statements
ip_top_stories.summary: Shareholders have filed a lawsuit against Adobe executives, alleging they made misleading statements about the copyright safety of AI-generated content produced using Adobe's tools. The case raises significant questions about corporate liability for AI copyright claims and the accuracy of representations made to investors about IP risk.

ip_top_stories.title: APRA AMCOS Reveals Australian And New Zealand Songs Found In AI Training Datasets
ip_top_stories.summary: Australian and New Zealand music rights organisation APRA AMCOS has revealed that songs from its members have been identified in AI training datasets, intensifying debate over unlicensed use of copyrighted music. The disclosure adds to growing pressure on AI developers to negotiate licensing agreements with rights holders.

ip_further_links.title: New Law Would Give Artists Sweeping Protections Against AI Stealing Their Work
ip_further_links.summary: A proposed US law would give artists broad rights to prevent AI systems from using their work without authorisation, marking one of the most expansive legislative proposals yet for protecting creative IP from AI training.

ip_further_links.title: The novel legal strategy that Taylor Swift and Matthew McConaughey are using to fight AI
ip_further_links.summary: A report on how high-profile celebrities including Taylor Swift and Matthew McConaughey are pursuing novel legal strategies—including rights of publicity and voice registration—to combat unauthorised AI use of their likenesses.

ip_further_links.title: Bombay High Court allows Preity Zinta to sue online platforms for infringement of content produced with AI
ip_further_links.summary: India's Bombay High Court has granted actor Preity Zinta permission to pursue legal action against major online platforms including Google and Meta over AI-related infringement of her likeness and content.

ip_further_links.title: Inside AIMP 2026: Glen Ballard and U.S. Copyright Office Leaders Debate A.I., Ownership, and the Future of Music Publishing
ip_further_links.summary: Music industry figures and US Copyright Office leaders debated AI ownership and the future of music publishing at the AIMP 2026 conference, highlighting unresolved questions around AI-generated music and rights.

ip_further_links.title: Grand Chamber rules that platform's algorithmic control may remove safe harbour availability
ip_further_links.summary: The IPKat reports on a Grand Chamber ruling finding that platforms exercising algorithmic control over content may lose safe harbour protections, with significant implications for AI-driven content moderation and copyright liability.

ip_further_links.title: AI-generated works raise new intellectual property questions
ip_further_links.summary: A general survey of the emerging IP questions posed by AI-generated works, covering authorship, ownership, and the adequacy of existing copyright frameworks.

ip_further_links.title: Protecting press copyright: Conditions for press to develop sustainably in the AI era
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of the conditions needed to protect press publishers' copyright as AI systems increasingly consume and reproduce news content without licensing agreements.

ip_further_links.title: Infringement risks of AIGC in the entertainment industry (Part 2)
ip_further_links.summary: A legal analysis of the copyright infringement risks arising from AI-generated content in the entertainment sector, examining liability frameworks and case precedents.

ip_further_links.title: Beijing International Book Fair Highlights Digital Publishing, Cross-Media Adaptations [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: The Beijing International Book Fair 2026 is focusing on publishing transformation, AI integration, and reading trends, reflecting the global publishing industry's ongoing engagement with digital and AI-driven change.

ip_further_links.title: Bigger verdicts, fewer injunctions: AI, telecoms, and trade secrets shake up litigation
ip_further_links.summary: A litigation trends report finds that AI-related cases are contributing to larger damages verdicts while courts are increasingly reluctant to grant injunctions, reshaping the IP litigation landscape.
